frameworks.title: Tones change meaning
frameworks.body: Mā (mother), má (hemp), mǎ (horse), mà (scold). Same syllable, four meanings. Tones aren't optional — they're the word.

frameworks.title: No verb conjugation
frameworks.body: Verbs don't change for tense or person. Time is shown with words like 昨天 (yesterday) or 了 (past marker).

frameworks.title: Measure words
frameworks.body: You can't say 'three book' — you need a measure word: 三本书 (three [volume] books).

primer.title: How Mandarin is written — and how you get in
primer.tagline: There is no alphabet. So we start with the one that was made for you.

facts.label: Characters
facts.text: Chinese is written in characters, each carrying meaning rather than sound. There is no alphabet to learn and no way to sound out a character you have never seen.

facts.label: Pinyin
facts.text: Pinyin spells Mandarin sounds in Latin letters. It is not Chinese writing — it is the ladder in, and it is what this course teaches first.

facts.label: Four tones
facts.text: The same syllable in a different pitch is a different word. mā is mother, mǎ is horse. Tone is not expression, it is part of the word.

facts.label: Characters have parts
facts.text: Most characters are built from a meaning component and a sound component. 妈 (mā, mother) is 女 'woman' plus 马 'mǎ'. Once you see this, characters stop being pictures to memorise.

primer.hardest: The tones, and the fact that pinyin letters do not say what an English speaker expects. q is roughly 'ch', x is roughly 'sh', and zh/ch/sh are said with the tongue curled back. Learn these four wrong and every word after them is wrong.
primer.firstWin: Mandarin grammar is startlingly simple — no verb conjugation, no plurals, no gender, no tenses. Nearly all the difficulty is in the sound and the script, and none of it is in the sentences.

confusables.tell: j is said with the tongue flat and forward. zh is the same sound with the tongue curled back.
Same pair again, aspirated: q is forward, ch is curled back.
And again: x is forward and hissy, sh is curled back.
Third tone dips down then rises. Fourth tone falls sharply, like an order.
